subject.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends

question: Should the supplied incident timeline, upstream `imsg` contract, deterministic 158-second regression, and fast-path patched-build run be accepted as the proof basis for this delayed-fallback timeout change, or should the PR require additional redacted runtime boundary diagnostics?
rationale: The changed user-visible path cannot be safely fault-injected in the stated production-like setup without risking real duplicate delivery, while the current live proof exercises only the unaffected fast bridge path.

options.title: Accept the bounded proof basis
options.body: Treat the documented dependency contract and deterministic delayed-boundary regression as sufficient, accepting up to 30 seconds of additional failure latency to avoid ambiguous successful sends.

options.title: Request explicit proof override or diagnostics
options.body: Require a clear maintainer proof override or safely redacted runtime diagnostics that connect the delayed fallback boundary to the patched timeout before merge.

recommendation.title: Request explicit proof override or diagnostics
recommendation.body: Require a clear maintainer proof override or safely redacted runtime diagnostics that connect the delayed fallback boundary to the patched timeout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available discussion contains the explicit delivery-versus-latency decision and the adjacent merged timeout design history.
